program: Whole organization; finite symptomatic dental relief quantified

nutshell.headline: Real dental delivery; patient volume and additional relief remain unmeasured
nutshell.body: The signed prior-weighted estimate is $2,041,966 per 10 Bay QALYs (0.048972 per $10,000 gift). It is a judgment-led exploratory estimate, not measured clinic QALYs.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Mobile treatment can shorten painful waits for patients who cannot obtain equivalent care promptly.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The favorable 10% world contributes 96.4% of signed expected benefit. Targets are not completions, and whole-org Bay share is unknown.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD a giving recommendation: actual annual treatment completion, local counterfactual access and cash-created capacity are unverified.

programSection.body: Health Mobile (EIN 31-1658149) reports seven mobile medical/dental units and a leased facility serving primarily uninsured low-income children throughout California. A current funder confirms San Jose dental treatment. This is not the similarly named Salinas Valley or other mobile-health programs.

steps.title: Retain whole cost
steps.detail: All medical, dental, education, administration and facility costs remain in denominator.

steps.title: Separate people from completed treatment
steps.detail: Annual person prior × uniqueness × completed-restorative share × symptomatic share.

steps.title: Estimate finite health beyond alternative care
steps.detail: Successful relief × utility × expected incremental painful time.

steps.title: Apply funding response, harms and Bay attribution
steps.detail: No rescue, mortality or lifetime credit. Publicly funded baseline is not automatically new donor impact.

programSection.boundary: Only finite symptomatic dental health is quantified. Primary medical care, nonpain dentistry, prevention, education, chewing and long-term tooth retention remain unquantified, with their costs retained. Complete societal resource cost is unknown: donated labor, partner support and capital may be absent from accounting.

model.headline: $2,041,966 per 10 Bay QALYs
model.body: A whole-cost/partial-health diagnostic, not a verified offer to purchase extra treatments. FY 2025 costs and current scale priors are not synchronized observed cost-effectiveness data.

equation.label: Signed incremental Bay health
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × annual people prior × funding × (unique × completed restorative share × symptomatic share × relief × utility × incremental years − harm/person) × Bay share

inputs.label: Whole historical organization expense
inputs.basis: Original FY ending June 2025 return, all functions retained. Not complete donated-resource cost.
inputs.confidence: High accounting; low current marginal relevance

inputs.label: Annual service-recipient equivalents before residual dedup
inputs.basis: Unknown actual annual whole-org volume. These are not observed unique annual people; the unique factor applies residual person/episode dedup. Central extrapolates modestly beyond one district target; neither 400 target nor 1500 services are measured completed treatment.

inputs.label: Unique person/episode adjustment
inputs.basis: Annual throughput is service-recipient equivalents before this residual dedup factor, not observed unique people. No procedure-to-person equivalence.

inputs.label: Completed restorative treatment share
inputs.basis: Removes screening, education, cleaning-only visits and incomplete courses. Service menu is not completed-case mix.

inputs.label: Symptomatic share among completed episodes
inputs.basis: Nonpain restorative/preventive care is not credited with immediate pain relief.

inputs.label: Successful symptomatic relief
inputs.basis: Provider 90% pain-free target is not evidence of causal relief or clinic quality; prior remains judgment.

inputs.label: Incremental utility while pain is relieved
inputs.basis: Analyst judgment, not direct EQ5D/OHIP/pain-scale conversion. Adult active-comparator study does not establish effect in children.

inputs.label: Expected incremental painful time
inputs.basis: Average time before equivalent alternative care or need resolution, including zero/prompt-alternative cases. Not tooth lifespan, nor a promise of three extra months for every patient.

inputs.label: Whole-gift capacity response
inputs.basis: Separate budget/capacity response. Public contracts, paid staff, van and clinic capacity can make a gift displace baseline or pay liabilities. No verified priced expansion.

inputs.label: Bay share of incremental health
inputs.basis: Statewide/Northern California service scope. San Jose and district locations confirm some Bay activity, not whole-org residence mix.

inputs.label: Harm QALY per additional person
inputs.basis: Independent hypothetical postoperative complications/access burdens not already netted in utility. No observed adverse-event rate.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Subjective world mass below $1 M/10:0.1; below $100 k/10:0. Not calibrated probabilities. Excluding and renormalizing favorable world:$51,249,226 per 10. Scenario coefficients and weights were saved before first evaluation; no threshold tuning.
model.fundingBoundary: Original FY 2025 revenue 343009 includes 69480 government grants and 165229 program revenue; full expense 363688 is not reduced by either. Staff costs 201343 and 7 employees contradict an assumed all-volunteer model. Cash 64992, assets 282070, liabilities 273183, net assets 8887. Net assets moved from −220434 through −20679 operating result plus 250000 prior-period correction; Schedule O calls this correction of an overstated 2024 liability, not fresh cash. All expense is classified as program by filer; zero reported functional overhead does not justify reducing whole cost. Current restricted funds, contract renewal conditions, donated resources and unit utilization remain unknown.

evidence.population: Whole legal organization, FY ending June 2025
evidence.result: Expense and revenue reconcile; liability correction explains net asset movement. No actual annual patients or completed procedures provided.
evidence.transfer: No cost-per-treatment can be called observed. Accounting liabilities and geography require whole-org interpretation.

evidence.population: District proposed dental program, not entire organization
evidence.result: 400 people/1500 services annual targets; 600 improved people inconsistent with 400 served; 90% no-pain is a target. Dual funding recommendation 110000; not a new private gap.
evidence.transfer: No measured pain-free rate, completion count or causal additionality. May 2026 search extraction repeats 400/1500 and corrects improved people to 400, but full newer packet was inaccessible and no actual outcome inferred.

evidence.population: San Jose low-income and unhoused patients
evidence.result: Fillings, root canals and extractions are real service offerings.
evidence.transfer: Does not establish completed annual mix or additional outcomes versus public/private alternatives.

evidence.design: Prospective nonrandomized controlled Swedish dental cohort
evidence.result: No significant intergroup QALY difference; approximately .83 QALYs each over one year. Before/after utility improvements are not untreated causal effects.
evidence.transfer: Study compares two treatments, not care versus no care. No direct .05 utility import; child-heavy and mobile-clinic transfer is especially uncertain.

evidence.population: Medi-Cal members, not measured Health Mobile patient insurance mix
evidence.result: Under 19 members retain full dental benefits; some adults transition to emergency-only coverage.
evidence.transfer: Neither nominal coverage nor uninsured label establishes actual timely alternative care; no change to locked coefficients.

reservations: No observed completed-treatment denominator: throughput and completion assumptions are independent weak links.
Public targets are not actuals, and metrics-met percentages do not reveal completed clinical episodes.
Cash shortage, staff bottlenecks and debt servicing are not interchangeable.
Statewide organization: do not assign 100% Bay solely from headquarters or current spotlight.
FY 2025 costs may understate or overstate FY 2026/27 service costs.
Utility, duration, relief and harm are analyst priors, not measured Health Mobile effects.
Societal resources and unquantified medical/preventive benefits remain outside the numeric health estimate.

DHCS confirms under 19 Medi-Cal members retain full dental benefits despite July 2026 restrictions for some adults. Child-heavy service is not automatically without covered alternatives; eligibility and timely access still vary.
excludedBenefits: Screening and education converted directly to QALYs
